about: T2c classes of Bolorgir errors in T8a on the core 9a5baf3e (t8a_report.py --t2c, run_t8a.sh T8A_T2C), prepared 2026-10-13 for the wheel bolorgir-0.2.0rc1-cp312-abi3-linux_x86_64.whl (sha256 b5635a7e...) built from the frozen sources of the release line with the in-tree core. No class is carried over from the 6e62e0d1 files: the classes for this core are prepared only from the outcomes measured in the first full run of the work dir benchmarks/local/t8a-work-9a5baf3e (the D4 decisions of the T3 review do not decide T8a errors). On 2026-10-13 class D was accepted for the four format-only instances of Github_easy---o76630.json (instance #1) and Github_medium---o6171.json (instances #2, #4, #7) on the basis of the diagnosis of that run; every other Bolorgir error, the timeouts of the run included, stays open because no entry covers it. A class covers only its file with the exact outcome it names as status, under the T8a protocol stated below (900 s per file, one worker, memory limit 40 GB, spec-v1, bolorgir, compact): the status timeout is a pending marker whose chunk ended with exit -14 (the runner's SIGALRM) while it ran the file; t8a_report.py applies the class only then, so a crash with another exit, a validation error or a marker without that chunk end stays open. The table status crash_or_timeout stays. A timeout of any other file is not covered and stays open. The causes inside the core are open. The protocol block states those limits in complete machine-readable form; t8a_report.py applies a class only when every required condition is present with the run's value, otherwise every case stays open.
decided: 2026-10-13: class D for the four format-only instances (Github_easy---o76630.json #1; Github_medium---o6171.json #2, #4, #7); every other error, every timeout and every future error stays open

Github_easy---o76630.json.note: divergence from the reference expectation, accepted as a documented limitation of spec-v1: the wrong acceptance is instance #1 (0-based; homePage, format iri, value "not-an-iri"); the ONLY violation is the format annotation, which spec-v1 never asserts (docs/dialect-matrix.md section 2 rule 5; docs/supported_features.md), so the acceptance is the documented behavior, not a regression. Reproduced with real format checkers: zero non-format errors, exactly one format error; T3 on the same core records the same acceptance with validator: true. The run record keeps only the last failing test; the instance list is the complete set enumerated from the streams and the reference (diag/wrong_instances.py).

Github_medium---o6171.json.note: divergence from the reference expectation, accepted as a documented limitation of spec-v1: the wrong acceptances are instances #2 (creationDate "2022-01-01 12:00:00"), #4 (creationDate "2022-01-01T12:00:00" without offset) and #7 (creationDate and lastUpdated "not a date") (0-based), each violating ONLY the date-time format annotation, which spec-v1 never asserts (docs/dialect-matrix.md section 2 rule 5; docs/supported_features.md); every instance violating an implemented keyword (pattern/enum) was rejected. Reproduced with real format checkers: zero non-format errors, only date-time format errors; T3 on the same core records the same acceptances with validator: true. The run record keeps only the last failing test (#7); the instance list is the complete set enumerated from the streams and the reference (diag/wrong_instances.py).
